title: Oncall handoff - Nadia Cho (Night Shift) - Draft
summary: Night shift handoff notes and temporary procedures. Contains quick checks, active incidents and escalation steps for redis-cluster flapping and hosted-api latency spike. Draft - will be cleaned up later.
shift_notes: Summary of what I saw during my shift: 1) Redis cluster started flapping between 03:20-03:48 UTC causing ~5% error-rate on hosted-api writes. Circuit broke on two replicas; primary failover succeeded automatically. I manually bumped instance count on redis-proxy-staging to mitigate. 2) Hosted API latency spike around 05:15 UTC correlated with high tail latencies on model-worker-gpu nodes in us-west-2; root cause appears to be a recent kernel update on a subset of nodes (k8s node images rolled with new nvidia driver). 3) No customer-facing incidents opened yet; monitoring alert thresholds were hit but auto-recovery completed. Notes to incoming oncall: watch Redis steady-state for 1 hour, monitor GPU node drain status and model-worker pod restarts.
active_incidents: INC-4215: redis-cluster flapping - currently stabilized; Redis primary shifted twice. PagerDuty: paged at 03:25 UTC. Owner: Samir Ali. Next steps: keep an eye on replica sync lag and run redis-check-sync.sh if lag > 10s.

INC-4218: hosted-api latency spike - payloads failed for some long-context requests between 05:10-05:25 UTC. Owner: Nadia Cho. Temporary mitigation: roll model-worker-gpu pool 2 with previous kernel image (rollback tag: gpu-node-img:v2026-02-10).
temporary_procedures: Temporary failover checklist: 1) If redis primary flaps again -> Trigger manual failover: run 'kubectl exec -n infra redis-operator -- redis-cli --failover'. 2) If replica sync lag persists > 15s for > 10m -> promote a healthy replica and open a JIRA INC ticket. 3) For GPU node kernel-related latency: rollback nodes with label 'gpu-upgrade=true' using 'k8s-rollback.sh --nodes-label gpu-upgrade=true --image gpu-node-img:v2026-02-10' and cordon/drain before replacing. 4) If hosted-api 95p latency > 5s for > 10m -> shift traffic to dedicated pool in eu-west-1 using traffic-shift playbook (confluence link below).
quick_checks:
Commands to run on incoming shift: - kubectl get pods -n serving --selector=app=model-worker -o wide
- kubectl top nodes | grep gpu
- redis-cli -h <redis-primary> INFO replication
- curl -sS https://api.internal.redwood/v1/_health | jq '.'
- grafana dashboard: /d/serving/hosted-api-overview (ensure retention from 02:00 UTC onward)
follow_up_actions: Raise a post-mortem for INC-4215 if we see > 1 flapping event in 24h
Validate kernel rollout plan for gpu nodes and hold next wave until root cause confirmed
Add an automated check to alert if redis replica lag > 10s longer than 5m
pagerduty: Primary schedule: SRE-Night (rotation). Escalation: Oncall -> Sr SRE -> Platform Eng lead. PD escalation policy: 30m initial, 15m escalations.
